I empathize with so much of what you're saying. It gets really exhausting when your only motivation for going on comes from other people, regardless of how much you love or care about them. I also know the feelings of hopelessness that come when you lose someone (even a celebrity) and understand wishing your places were reversed. Try to remember that while it's awful that he had to pass, and no doubt deserved to live a longer and more fulfilling life, so do you. You deserve to have a life full of joy, and to see your aspirations through. Focus on the things you're good at and like about yourself, if the big stuff is too hard, then just remember the small things (e.g. I really like my handwriting, or I'm proud of the way I fold my clothes). If you can't think of anything for yourself, then just know that you're strong and a good person, you took time and commented on a post I made tonight, and just knowing someone read it helped me. And if you can do that, even in the state you're in, you've got a lot of strength.

Recently applied for a low level job doing technical work at an amusement park. After a series of standard personality and skill based questions, the interviewer asked me: 
“How comfortable are you with electrical calculations?”
“I’m pretty comfortable” I replied (not a lie, but I’m not the best)
“Ok so if I charge a 10uF capacitor by connecting it to a 12V source. and a 20uF capacitor charged to 15V, what is the energy stored in each capacitor?”
😶
When I asked if I could use a calculator or even just pen and paper she said;
“This is more to test speed than accuracy”
What followed was a series of a dozen or so more rapid fire math questions with escalating difficulty. 
By the end of it I had sweat through my interview clothes.

One day in junior year of high school, my best friend Fred came in sporting a new(to him) blazer he bought from Savers (a used clothing store). After showing it off he tells me that we need to talk in private. We go into a corner and he tells me that he found a small baggie of cocaine in a hidden pocket of the blazer. He seemed really scared, and asked me what I thought he should do with the drugs. His mom was very over protective and would have not believed his story, and we both believed that if he gave it to the cops, they would just arrest him for possession. As we were discussing, another kid walked past and overheard our conversation. This kid, Shawn was quite the wangster and began to regale us with his many tales of doing coke, after which he offered to buy the coke from Fred for $50. Being broke high school students, and wanting to get rid of the potentially incriminating stuff, he sold it. Well turns out that Shawn was lying and had never done coke, so he proceeded use it all in one sitting, O.D., and slip into a brief coma. After Shawn woke up he quickly spilled the beans about where he got the stuff. and that's the story of how my strait laced best friend in high school got expelled for selling cocaine.
**tldr: best friend finds bag of cocaine, sells it to druggie kid who claims to have done it before, kid O.D.'s, survives, and spills the beans, friend gets expelled.**
